_comment: Which template files have actually RUN inside a real project, as opposed to
merely existing here and looking finished.
Written after suite-lock.mjs shipped with a deadlock on 3 September 2026. Its
own tests were green, but they only covered cases its author had thought of;
the case that broke it was already sitting in the project it was written for,
and adoption found it in minutes. The drift checker could say a file was
missing from a project. Nothing could say it had never been run anywhere.
The default is unproven. A file absent from `proven` below is reported as
never having run, so silence means not-yet-trusted rather than fine.
The bar is narrow on purpose: a file is proven when ITS OWN TESTS RAN GREEN
inside a real project's suite. Being copied in is not proof, and neither is
being read and approved. Record it with:
node ~/.claude/bin/record-safety-net-proof.mjs <file> <project> "<what ran>"
Provenance is per file, not per version. Whoever changes a file materially
removes its entry, which is the same judgment the copy-improvements-back rule
already asks for.
Entries marked backfilled were not observed being recorded; they were
reconstructed on 3 September 2026 from what is checkable now. They are the
weakest entries here and should be replaced by an observed run when one
happens, rather than trusted as if someone had watched them pass.

24 September 2026: run-tests-unless-docs.mjs, project-root.mjs and suite-lock.mjs were changed materially (the test hooks now follow the work into git worktrees, and the suite lock is shared per repository), so their entries were removed per the rule above. Their new tests ran green only in a scratch copy, which is not a real project's suite. They are unproven until adopted and seen green in one.

protect-paths.mjs.how: backfilled: present there with protect-paths.test.ts alongside it, last touched on this date, and that project's suite was green at 1730 on 3 Sept 2026

project-root.mjs.how: Post-merge live check 24 Sept 2026, IPG main e6e0e68: a real harness-fired edit in a worktree recorded that worktree for the session; the finish hook run from main then ran the full suite in the worktree, 2040/2040 across 170 files, and a second finish ran nothing.
